realism.how: A parcel handed in at the post office in 1989: the sender wrapped the goods in brown paper and tied them with string themselves, because the state post required a firm tied packet, and a blank address card or label went on top. Cardboard moving boxes were not for the post.
realism.current: Paper and string was how every local sent a parcel that year; a plastic mailer bag or a courier box with tape would be from a later decade.
